originalTitle: Global Market: AI investment story shifts from spending to picking the winners
simplifiedContent: Here's a simplified version of the news: The conversation around investing in Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing. Instead of just focusing on spending money on AI, investors are now trying to figure out which companies will be the most successful in the long run. Companies that make semiconductors, provide cloud services, and have strong financials are still expected to do well. Investors are now prioritizing which companies can make a profit, have reasonable valuations, and control their own infrastructure. This shift in focus may help investors pick the winners in the AI industry.

originalTitle: Global Market: Emerging Asian currencies rise as softer dollar supports regional markets
simplifiedContent: The value of currencies in some Asian countries, like Taiwan and Thailand, went up on Monday. This happened because the value of the US dollar went down, which helped the Asian markets. Investors were also keeping an eye on some important economic news, such as Japan's slow growth and upcoming decisions from banks in Indonesia. This news is important because it can affect the overall performance of the markets in Asia. It shows that the value of the US dollar and other economic factors can have a big impact on the Asian markets.

originalTitle: Anthropic IPO valuation hinges on $190-200 billion 2028 revenue forecast: Report
simplifiedContent: Here's a simplified version of the news item: Anthropic, an artificial intelligence company, is preparing to go public and investors are trying to figure out how much the company is worth. The company thinks it will make $190-200 billion in revenue by 2028, which is a very big increase. This forecast is important because it helps investors decide if they want to invest in the company. Investors are comparing Anthropic to similar companies like Palantir and SpaceX to help them make their decision. The company's expected growth and big investments in its operations are key factors in determining its value.

originalTitle: Baazar Style Retail shares hit 5% upper circuit on reports of Aditya Halwasia buying company shares worth  ₹163 crore
simplifiedContent: Bazaar Style Retail's stock price rose sharply, reaching its highest allowed limit of 5% in one day. This happened after news came out that Aditya Halwasia bought a significant amount of the company's shares, worth about ₹163 crore. The shares started the day at ₹384.45, which is higher than their previous closing price of ₹366.15 on the last trading day of the previous week. This sudden increase in the stock price could be a sign that investors are becoming more interested in the company. The purchase by Aditya Halwasia may have triggered this increase in the stock price.

originalTitle: Pramodini Medicare IPO allotment in focus today; latest GMP, 5 steps to check status
simplifiedContent: The company Pramodini Medicare had an Initial Public Offering (IPO), which means they sold shares of their company to the public. Today, they decided who gets to buy those shares, which is called the allotment. If you invested in the IPO, you can check if you got any shares on a website called Purva Sharegistry. People who didn't get shares will get their money back starting tomorrow, and those who did get shares will have them added to their accounts tomorrow as well. The shares will start trading on a stock exchange called NSE SME on August 19.

originalTitle: Sunshine Pictures IPO: GMP signals 15% listing pop; dates, price band, other key details in 10 points
simplifiedContent: The company Sunshine Pictures is going public, which means it's allowing people to buy its shares for the first time. The initial public offering (IPO) will start on August 18 and end on August 20. The price of each share will be between ₹342 and ₹360. This is the "price band" set by the company, which means you can buy shares within this price range. The company's shares are expected to increase in value by 15% on the first day of trading, which is a good sign for investors.
